provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after quaesumus; 1862 sets no comma after ut; 1862 spells exequentes and majora where the 1962 spells exsequentes and maiora (orthography); 1862 sets a comma after exequentes where the 1962 sets a semicolon. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 40306-40310 prints the whole prayer, and the 1570 at lines 56258-56264 prints it as well. Recorded limitation: THREE WORDS INFERRED, NOT READ, AND SAID SO. The 1862 text layer damages three words in this short prayer: line 52750 reads 'finctum' for fructum, line 52751 reads 'exe<iu6ntes' for exequentes, and lines 52752-52753 break percipiant as 'per- / dpiant'. I did not repair any of them silently. All three are supplied from the 1604 at lines 40306-40310, which prints 'Excita, quaesumus Domine, tuorum fidelium voluntates: vt diuini operis fructu propensius exequentes, pietatis tuae remedia maiora percipiant. Per Dominu.' at the same place in the same formulary, and the 1570 agrees at lines 56258-56264. Confidence is medium because three of this prayer's words rest on that inference rather than on a clean 1862 reading. Note also that the 1604 and 1570 both set a comma after exequentes as the 1862 does, so the 1962 semicolon is the innovation and it is pointing only. The 1862 reading rests on the text layer alone.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after et and instead sets one after oblationibus, where the 1962 does the reverse; 1862 sets a colon after converte where the 1962 sets a semicolon; 1862 sets no comma after ut; 1862 spells coelestia where the 1962 spells caelestia (oe/ae orthography); 1862 conclusion is the short cue Per Dominum. where the 1962 prints Per Dominum nostrum.. Corroboration: 1604 at lines 40376-40385 prints the whole prayer: 'Propitius esto Domine, supplicationibus nostris: & populi tui oblationibus, precibusq. susceptis, omnium nostrum ad te corda conuerte; vt a terrenis cupiditatibus liberati, ad caelestia desideria transeamus. Per Dominum.'. Recorded limitation: TWO WORDS INFERRED, NOT READ. The 1862 layer damages supplicationibus at lines 52894-52895, which recognise as '"pRopftius esto,D6mine, sup- / JT nlicati6nibus nostris' where the ornamental P has eaten the pl of supplicationibus; and it damages omnium at line 52897, which reads '6mmum'. Line 52899 also reads 'terr&ris' for terrenis. All three are supplied from the 1604 at lines 40376-40382, which prints this prayer whole at the same place. I record the layer as it reads and set confidence to medium for that reason. The pointing of this prayer differs between the two books in four places, all of them commas and colons, and no word differs. The 1862 reading rests on the text layer alone.
